note: Recast from the genus-level monograph description of Roonwal & Chhotani (1989), in English, which is itself recast from the original description of Desneux 1904 and the redescription of Roonwal & Sen-Sarma (1960); the alate, soldier and pseudoworker are all described and measured, the first two from Sri Lankan material from the Kandy area. Synonym: Calotermes militaris ab. unidentatus Kemner, 1926.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head, pronotum and body reddish brown; antennae, legs, sternites, wing scales and costal margin of the wings pale brown; wings pale yellow. Head and body sparsely hairy. Body length about 10.0—12.0 mm (without wings), 19.0—20.5 mm (with wings). Head capsule suboval, the maximum width including the compound eyes almost equal to the length to the mandibular base (width 1.90—1.95, length 1.40—1.70 mm); Y suture absent or indistinct. Compound eyes large, black, circular, maximum diameter including the eye facets 0.45—0.50 mm. Ocelli oval, semitransparent, almost touching the eye facets. Antenna hairy, 19—20 segments; segments 2 and 3 nearly equal in length, segment 4 shorter than segment 3. Anteclypeus trapezoidal, whitish; postclypeus darker than the rest of the head, weakly convex anteriorly and strongly convex posteriorly. Labrum subsquare, the sides nearly parallel; length 0.45, width 0.50—0.55 mm, with a few hairs at the apex. Mandibles of the typical Postelectrotermes type. Pronotum subrectangular, much wider than the head width including the compound eyes; length 1.3—1.4, width 2.10—2.20 mm; anterior margin broadly incurved, posterior margin nearly straight with a shallow median concavity. Legs long and slender, hairy; apical tibial spur formula 3:3:3, the outer side of the middle tibia with a stout spine above the spur; an arolium between the claws. Wings hairy, tuberculate; forewing length including the wing scale 17.2—17.6, hindwing length 15.5—15.6 mm; forewing scale larger than the hindwing scale; venation as in the genus. The microsculpture of the wing membrane consists of tubercles, with a density per square millimetre at the middle of the membrane of 9 in the forewing and 20 in the hindwing. Abdomen slender and long, hairy; cerci short, 2-segmented, hairy.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule brown to pale chestnut brown, the frons darker; antennal base brown, the apex paler; labrum pale brown; pronotum, legs and body yellowish white. Head and body sparsely hairy. Body length about 10.5—11.0 mm. Head capsule subrectangular, the sides parallel; length to the mandibular base 2.88—3.31, width 1.80—2.34 mm; posterior part rounded; frons sloping forwards, with a shallow depression extending backwards to the occiput; Y suture not visible. Compound eyes suboval, semitransparent, elongate, maximum diameter 0.24 mm; the distance to the antennae slightly less than their maximum diameter. Ocelli absent. Antenna 16—18 segments, fairly densely hairy, segments 2 and 3 nearly equal in length, segment 4 the shortest. Anteclypeus trapezoidal, whitish, hairless. Postclypeus subrectangular, darker than the frons, with 2 pairs of hairs on the anterior margin. Labrum subsquare, length 0.30—0.54, width 0.54—0.60 mm; anterior margin with a weak pointed median process, the surface with a few hairs. Mandibles long and slender, nearly straight, weakly incurved apically, not swollen at the base; length equal to or greater than half the head length; left mandible length 1.62—1.89 mm, mandible length/head length index 0.51—0.64. Left mandible with 4 and right mandible with 2 marginal teeth. Postmentum long, club-shaped, widest before the posterior half, narrowed in the middle and slightly widened again at the base; the wider anterior part bilobed; anterior margin rounded, posterior margin nearly straight. Pronotum subrectangular, maximum length 0.95—1.20, maximum width 1.98—2.46 mm, about as wide as the head; anterior margin shallowly concave, posterior margin nearly straight. Legs long and slender, sparsely hairy; femora not swollen, apical tibial spur formula 3:3:3, the outer side of the middle tibia with a stout spine above the spur; tarsi 4-segmented. Abdomen elongate-oval; each tergite with 2 rows of hairs; cerci 2-segmented, hairy.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Pseudoworker: head capsule and labrum straw-coloured; mandibles also straw-coloured, the dentate margins brownish; antennae, pronotum, legs and body yellowish white. Head and body fairly hairy. Body length about 7.0—8.0 mm. Head capsule subcircular, head length to the mandibular base 1.6—1.7, width 1.6—1.8 mm; hairs medium; frons weakly sloping anteriorly, with a median concavity. Compound eyes degenerate, small white circular pits flush with the head surface. Ocelli absent. Antenna 15—17 segments, hairy; segments 3—5 the shortest. Anteclypeus trapezoidal, white; postclypeus rectangular, flat, darker than the frons, with 2 pairs of hairs on the anterior margin. Labrum subsquare, widest in the middle; apex and surface hairy. Mandibles as in the alate. Pronotum wider than the head, width 1.8—2.2, length 0.9—1.3 mm; anterior margin deeply concave, without a median notch; posterior margin straight. Legs and abdomen as in the soldier.
